mathematical_boundaries: The distinction between a non-Kahler ambient manifold and a nonclosed background remains central. The lower-volume topology is completely metrizable without claiming that its original comparison satisfies the triangle inequality. Its complete metric keeps Cauchy sequences away from zero lower volume; the curve metric instead includes zero model volume in a fixed positive background. General finite-measure equations distinguish the semipositive-big/positive-lower-mass/smaller-background-reference regime from arbitrary smooth big backgrounds with bounded mass and positive lower model volume. A relative-envelope conclusion is not replaced by bounded difference. Scalar uniqueness, bounded potential uniqueness and approximation selection remain separate. The pole discussion distinguishes descent of the full logarithmic potential from descent of its bounded residual. Holder distance control is not extended to all bounded or continuous potentials, and a density vanishing order alone does not determine regularity or completeness.
